root_cause.text: Memory leak in the Versal NET EDAC driver because a dynamically allocated device name (via kzalloc) is assigned to `dev->init_name`, but after `device_register()` copies the name and sets `dev->init_name` to NULL, the original dynamically allocated pointer becomes unreachable and is never freed, even on the normal removal path.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states: "The device name allocated via kzalloc() in init_one_mc() is assigned to dev->init_name but never freed on the normal removal path. device_register() copies init_name and then sets dev->init_name to NULL, so the name pointer becomes unreachable from the device. Thus leaking memory." The patch replaces `kzalloc(MC_NAME_LEN, GFP_KERNEL)` with a stack-local `char name[MC_NAME_LEN]` and removes the `kfree(name)` error path and the `err_name_free` label.

vuln_statements.content: mci = edac_mc_alloc(i, ARRAY_SIZE(layers), layers, sizeof(struct mc_priv));
